title: acre animates how sufr builds a suffix array
body:
An animation, `figures/sufr-build.acre` in the acre checkout (kept out of git like every figure), that explains how sufr builds a suffix array. It runs at 1920 by 1080 for MP4 export, and its timeline marks each stage with a `section`.

sufr at 96bd1cc builds in `libsufr/src/build.rs`. It joins the FASTA records with `%` and appends `$`, folds lowercase, keeps the suffixes `starts` allows, packs the first 21 ranks of each suffix into a 64-bit key, counts suffixes per 5-character bucket, cuts the buckets into partitions, gathers each partition's suffixes in turns that the memory budget sets, sorts each partition by key with an LCP-aware merge sort for equal keys, and writes each partition straight to its slots. `tmp-claude/2026-11-23-sufr-animation/` holds a probe that runs libsufr on the examples and a Python model of keys, buckets and partitions.

## Sections

1. What a suffix array is, on a tiny text.
2. From FASTA to text: `>a ACGTN` and `>b acgTA` become `ACGTN%ACGTA$`.
3. Which suffixes: every one by default, or with `--dna` the ones starting with A, C, G or T, plus `$`.
4. Keys: the rank table and 3-bit packing into 64 bits.
5. Buckets and counting.
6. Partitions: whole buckets, cut by a running share of the suffixes.
7. Turns: the memory budget sets how many partitions are gathered per rescan of the text.
8. Sorting each partition by key, with the LCP from the keys.
9. Ties: a second text with a repeat longer than 21 characters, sorted by the LCP-aware merge.
10. Seed masks: a mask such as `1101` compares only care positions, and ties go by position descending, so the shortest suffix comes first.
11. Writing the `.sufr` file: partitions to their slots, boundary LCPs patched, header last.

Every value on screen comes from running libsufr or from the model checked against it.
close_reason: Jack: the sufr animation is not an acre project. The draft stays at figures/sufr-build.acre in the acre checkout, outside git; the acre gaps it found were filed and fixed here.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/0c799e42
notes.text: First full draft at `figures/sufr-build.acre`: 1920 by 1080, 280 s, eleven sections with subsections, all checked with `acre check` after `acre fmt`. `tmp-claude/2026-11-23-sufr-animation/values.md` names the probe run behind every value on screen. The ties example is a second, 75-character text of three records that share a 23-character run, and its equal-key run is 0, 25 and 50. The seed-mask section uses a third text, `ACCTN%ACGTA$`, because mask `1101` on the main text changes only LCPs. The draft worked around four acre gaps, filed as acre-36d52f, acre-b197ef, acre-f3d5fd and acre-42bcb1. Not yet done: review by Jack, and an MP4 export.
